messages.content: Write the opening pitch section of a README for a new open source charting library. Around 200 words.

output:
# Sparkplug

Charting libraries make you pick a side. Either you get twelve chart types with a theme picker and no escape hatch, or you get d3 and a free weekend.

Sparkplug sits in between. It ships a small set of marks — line, bar, area, point, rule — plus a layout engine that puts them on scales you control. Everything past that is composition. Want a candlestick? That's a rule and a bar sharing an x-scale. Nobody had to add it for you first.

The whole thing is 14 kB gzipped, no dependencies. It renders to SVG on the server and hydrates only the parts that answer a pointer, so a static dashboard ships zero JavaScript. Axis labels, tooltips, and legends are real DOM nodes, which means screen readers, ctrl-F, and browser zoom keep working the way they already did.

There is no config object with 200 keys. There's a function per mark, and the arguments are the ones you'd guess.

MIT-licensed. Works with React, Svelte, Vue, or plain HTML — the core doesn't know which one you picked, and doesn't care.

---

~200 words. The name and the two hard numbers (14 kB, the mark list) are placeholders — swap in your real figures, since the pitch leans on them being true.
